best_for: Home and office users who scan stacks of paper to searchable PDF and want one free tool that works with almost any scanner.
description:
NAPS2, short for Not Another PDF Scanner, is free scanning software from developer Ben Olden-Cooligan, with its code on GitHub. The goal is to get paper into a file with as few steps as possible.

It works with scanners from Canon, Brother, HP, Epson, Fujitsu and other brands. Before a scan you can set the DPI, page size and bit depth. If your scanner only does one side at a time, manual duplex joins the fronts and backs into one document. After the scan you can fix brightness and contrast. The app comes in more than 40 languages, and developers can build scanning into their own .NET programs with the NAPS2.Sdk library.

points.title: Scan to PDF, then fix the pages
points.text: NAPS2 scans from the flatbed or feeder, with duplex, then lets you reorder, rotate, crop and deskew pages before saving as PDF, TIFF, JPEG or PNG.

points.title: Searchable PDFs in 100+ languages
points.text: Built-in OCR turns scans into text you can search and copy.

points.title: Works with WIA, TWAIN and network scanners
points.text: On Windows it talks to WIA and TWAIN drivers, and ESCL lets it reach many network scanners with no driver at all. You can also share a scanner over your local network.

points.title: Free for business too
points.text: NAPS2 is GPL-2.0, free for people and companies, with no ads or bundled software. Admins get an MSI, group policy support, a command line and a portable zip.

points.title: Older Macs stay on 8.6.0
points.text: The download page sends macOS 12 and 13 to 8.6.0, and macOS 10.15 and 11 to 7.5.3. Windows 7 and 8 also stop at 7.5.3.

points.title: Versions kept here
points.text: Windows installs machine-wide, in x64 and Arm64, and the Windows listing keeps 33 versions. Mac has Intel and Apple Silicon packages with only the current release listed. Linux .deb, .rpm and Flatpak builds come from naps2.com.
